course.title: AI for DevOps on Azure: From Fundamentals to Production
course.subtitle: Deploy models in Microsoft Foundry, build RAG with Azure AI Search and run troubleshooting agents, with Terraform, Docker, Entra ID and a clean exit every time.
course.description:
On Azure, an AI feature is a model deployment, a search index, an identity, a quota and a bill. This course teaches you to build all of it and run it like the rest of your platform.

## What you'll build
- **Your first Foundry model:** resources, a deployment and a call from code, with keys kept out of the code.
- **A full-stack AI chat app:** React, Express and nginx in Docker Compose against a Microsoft Foundry model, then the same with Terraform.
- **A RAG system on Azure:** Blob Storage, Azure AI Search and a Foundry model, created with Terraform, answering with sources and refusing what the documents don't cover.
- **A self-hosted RAG stack** with per-user permissions and observability, to compare with the managed version.
- **Troubleshooting agents** that ask for approval before every fix: Docker skill agents and a Kubernetes doctor that runs on AKS.
- **Your own MCP server** in Python, connected to real AI agents.

## Prompt engineering: talk to AI like a professional
Most people use AI tools without knowing how to give them instructions. This course teaches prompting as an engineering skill: context, requirements, constraints, deliverables and acceptance criteria, then checking the answer instead of trusting it.
- **Available now:** how you talk to a model (system prompt, tokens, context window, temperature, structured output), judging answers (hallucination, grounding, citations, golden sets), and instruction files for AI coding agents: what to put in them, how they load, and permissions that really block an agent.
- **Coming next (in production now, added as each lesson is finished):** poor versus professional prompts run side by side; zero-, one- and few-shot, structured JSON output, task decomposition and prompt chaining; master prompts and reusable templates; the same prompt across Microsoft Foundry, ChatGPT, Claude and local Ollama models; prompting for Terraform, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, log analysis and incident reports, with every result validated; AI coding agents that plan, branch, test and ask before risky changes; building a reusable DevOps AI agent; grounded RAG prompts with citations; prompt security; and a downloadable Prompt Engineering Toolkit of templates and checklists.

## LLMOps: run AI applications in production
Building an AI app is the start; operating it is the job. This course treats LLMOps as a core skill, the way DevOps treats running any service.
- **Available now:** what LLMOps is and how it differs from DevOps and MLOps, the four LLMOps pipelines (ingestion, deployment, evaluation, observability), who builds and who runs an AI system, managed versus self-hosted models, operating and securing AI (versions, latency, token cost, drift, prompt injection, least privilege), a production-style RAG stack with Prometheus, Loki, Jaeger and Grafana, and AI in your CI/CD pipeline.
- **Coming next (in production now, added as each lesson is finished):** prompt versioning in Git with rollback, automated LLM evaluation that blocks a bad prompt in a pull request, LLM observability with Langfuse and OpenTelemetry (traces, tokens, latency, cost), caching, fallbacks and cost control, CI/CD and Kubernetes deployment for LLM apps, and an end-to-end LLMOps project on Microsoft Foundry, Azure Monitor and Application Insights, managed identities and Key Vault.

## Build websites and digital products with AI
DevOps engineers no longer need to wait for a developer to turn an idea into a working website. In this module you use AI to plan, design, build and ship it, then host it on Azure with your own domain and HTTPS, and keep it running with CI/CD.
- **Available now:** a full-stack AI chat app (React, Express and nginx in Docker Compose) on Microsoft Foundry, tested in the browser and built again with Terraform.
- **Coming next (in production now, added as each lesson is finished):** from business idea to requirements with AI; "build me a website" versus a professional master prompt; a professional business website and your DevOps portfolio built with an AI coding agent; hosting on Azure Static Web Apps; custom domains and HTTPS with Azure DNS and managed certificates; App Service and Container Apps for dynamic sites; CI/CD for website changes; website security; contact-form automation with n8n; an AI-powered business site with a RAG support chatbot; an online store and a subscription SaaS app in Stripe test mode; a business directory capstone; and ten downloadable website templates.
- Honest about the business side: you learn the skills and the responsibilities (costs, security, privacy, maintenance). No income promises.

## Why this course
- **Every lab runs for real** in your own Azure subscription with a budget alert first, and you delete exactly what you created.
- **Built for operations:** Entra ID over keys, content filters on, quotas and model retirements planned for.
- **Concepts first, in plain words,** then the Azure portal and code.
- **Labs and quizzes** for every hands-on lesson.

## Who it's for
DevOps, cloud and platform engineers who know Azure basics and Docker, and want to build, secure and operate AI applications on Azure.
objectives: Explain models, tokens, context windows, hallucinations and agents well enough to design AI features
Navigate the Azure AI ecosystem and choose between Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Search and task services
Deploy a model in Microsoft Foundry and call it from an application without exposing keys
Deploy a containerised AI chat app with Docker Compose and Terraform
Build a RAG system with Blob Storage, Azure AI Search and a Foundry model that cites its sources
Build troubleshooting agents that propose fixes, wait for approval, verify and report, on AKS or locally
Write an MCP server and connect AI agents to it safely
Operate AI in production: versions, evaluation, freshness, prompt injection, cost and least privilege
requirements: An Azure subscription where you can create resource groups, with a budget alert
Python or JavaScript reading skills for the labs (no ML background needed)

lessons.title: How computers solved problems before AI
lessons.summary: See how rule-based programs work, why most of the software you run still works that way, and where hand-written rules break down: everyday language, images and cases nobody planned for.

lessons.title: A short history of AI, from rules to agents
lessons.summary: Seventy years of AI in one walk: expert systems, machine learning, deep learning, chat assistants and agents, and what each step means for your work as a DevOps engineer.

lessons.title: What machine learning is: a spam filter, step by step
lessons.summary: Learn machine learning with one example, a spam filter: training on examples, inference with a probability, and how the same idea routes alerts and spots unusual metrics.

lessons.title: AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI
lessons.summary: The big words, one at a time: artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, generative and predictive AI, and where you meet each one as a DevOps engineer.

lessons.title: DevOps, MLOps, LLMOps, RAG and agentic AI, sorted
lessons.summary: Five terms people mix up, sorted into practices, an architecture and an application type, so you can tell DevOps, MLOps, LLMOps, RAG and agentic AI apart in any conversation.

lessons.title: Models: parameters, training, inference and model cards
lessons.summary: What an LLM is, parameters, pre-training, fine-tuning, inference, the knowledge cut-off, model cards, and open versus closed models: what to check before you deploy one.

lessons.title: Hallucinations, grounding and judging AI answers
lessons.summary: Fluent is not correct. Learn hallucination, grounding, citations, groundedness, evaluation and the golden set, and how to measure whether an AI answer can be trusted.

lessons.title: Running models: GPUs, VRAM, quantisation and licences
lessons.summary: What it takes to run a model yourself: runtime versus model, GPUs and VRAM, parameters and quantisation, self-hosted versus managed, and open source versus open weights.

lessons.title: Prompts, tokens, context windows and temperature
lessons.summary: The words every model call uses: prompt, system prompt, tokens, context window, temperature, max tokens, streaming and structured output, and how each changes the answer and the bill.

lessons.title: Agent instruction files in depth: how CLAUDE.md tells a coding agent your rules
lessons.summary: How a coding agent learns your build commands, conventions and mistakes to avoid: where instruction files live, the order they load, imports and rules, and what to put in or keep out. The same thinking applies to AGENTS.md and other agents.

lessons.title: Write instruction files for a coding agent, live
lessons.summary: On a real sample repository, generate a first instruction file, trim it, add rules and an import, then check exactly what the agent loads and when. The lab gives you the repository and the finished files.

lessons.title: Set an AI coding agent's permissions and project settings
lessons.summary: Global versus project settings for a coding agent: what goes where, which wins, what goes into Git, and a live proof that a deny rule really blocks the agent from running a command.

lessons.title: The Azure AI services map
lessons.summary: The whole Azure AI ecosystem, including the recent renames: what each service does, how they work together, a DevOps example of each and where to find them in the portal.

lessons.title: Choosing the right AI service on AWS or Azure
lessons.summary: A few questions that pick the right service for a job, real DevOps scenarios, and the traps that cost money: task service, model platform or your own model.

lessons.title: Microsoft Foundry explained
lessons.summary: Microsoft's platform for models and agents: resources, projects and deployments, Entra ID authentication, quotas, costs, content filters and model retirements. The video calls it Azure AI Foundry; Microsoft has since renamed it Microsoft Foundry.

lessons.title: Deploy your first model in Microsoft Foundry
lessons.summary: Give an AI ops assistant its brain on Azure: create the resources in the portal, deploy and test a model, call it from code, keep keys out of the code, then delete the resource group. Microsoft has since renamed it Microsoft Foundry.

lessons.title: Fix a 3 a.m. outage the classic way
lessons.summary: Follow an on-call engineer through a real nginx outage without any AI: reproduce it, read the logs and config, check the docs, fix it and update the runbook. Then do it yourself in the lab.

lessons.title: The same outage, fixed with an AI helper on Amazon Bedrock
lessons.summary: Replay the 3 a.m. 502 with an AI helper on Amazon Bedrock: what gets faster, what doesn't, and why the engineer still reviews every step. Then run it yourself in the lab. Shown with Amazon Bedrock; the same pattern works with Microsoft Foundry, which you use from module 4 on.

sections.title: Build and ship websites with AI

lessons.title: Deploy a full-stack AI chat app on Microsoft Foundry
lessons.summary: A React front end, an Express back end and nginx in Docker Compose, talking to a model you deploy in Microsoft Foundry: the key stays on the server, tested in the browser, built again with Terraform.

lessons.title: Preparing knowledge for RAG: parsing, chunks and indexing
lessons.summary: Follow one question through the first phase of RAG: the corpus, parsing, metadata, chunks and overlap, ingestion and indexing, and the first thing to check when an answer is missing.

lessons.title: Embeddings and vectors: matching meaning, not words
lessons.summary: How embeddings place similar meanings close together, what vectors, dimensions and similarity are, and why chunks and questions must use the same embedding model.

lessons.title: RAG search: keyword, vector, hybrid and reranking
lessons.summary: What happens when a question arrives: keyword, vector and hybrid search, top K, rerankers, query rewriting, and the difference between RAG and fine-tuning.

lessons.title: Where RAG data lives: object storage and vector databases
lessons.summary: Object storage, vector databases, index records and metadata filters: where a RAG system keeps its data, how permissions are enforced, and how to choose a store your team can run.

lessons.title: One RAG architecture, three implementations
lessons.summary: Self-hosted with Docker, on Azure and on AWS: three RAG systems that do the same six jobs with different names on the boxes, so every platform feels familiar.

lessons.title: Run a production-style RAG chatbot with Docker Compose
lessons.summary: Twenty-one containers answering from a company's own documents with sources, per-user document permissions and full observability in Grafana, on your computer or a VM.

lessons.title: Build a RAG system on Azure with Terraform
lessons.summary: Blob Storage, Azure AI Search and a Microsoft Foundry model, created with Terraform: answers from a school's documents with sources, refusals for what they don't cover, then destroy.

lessons.title: AI agents: tools, the agent loop, memory and guardrails
lessons.summary: A chatbot answers, an agent acts. Tools, function calling, MCP, the agent loop, memory, multiple agents, the human in the loop and guardrails, with the DevOps limits that keep agents safe.

lessons.title: AI chatbot versus AI agent, side by side
lessons.summary: Same model, same question: a chatbot that answers and an agent that acts. See how each works, what each can do, when to use which, and the guardrails an agent needs. Lab included.

lessons.title: Skill-based agents: one job, clear limits
lessons.summary: Why DevOps agents should have one skill each: investigate, propose a fix, wait for your approval, verify and report, and fail safely when they can't.

lessons.title: Three skill agents fix 502s, crash loops and full disks
lessons.summary: Three single-skill agents investigate, propose a fix, wait for your yes, apply it, verify and report: a 502 Bad Gateway, a container crash loop and a full disk.

lessons.title: An AI agent that fixes Kubernetes workloads
lessons.summary: An agent scans a namespace, finds broken workloads, fixes them one at a time with your approval, verifies and writes a report. Works on minikube, EKS or AKS.

lessons.title: AI agents inside Kubernetes with kagent
lessons.summary: kagent runs AI agents as Kubernetes resources: Agent, ModelConfig and MCP tools, deployed with kubectl and Helm, limited by RBAC and approvals.

lessons.title: Where AI fits in a CI/CD pipeline
lessons.summary: Map a real pipeline: where an AI helper speeds up builds, tests, reviews and fixes, where a human must still say yes, and how fixes arrive as pull requests, GitOps included.

lessons.title: Deployment notifications from CI with n8n
lessons.summary: Your pipeline calls an n8n webhook after each deployment and the team sees a green or red message in Mattermost, protected by a token. The lab starts n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose.

lessons.title: Send GitHub pull request updates to your team chat
lessons.summary: Turn every pull request event (opened, updated, reviewed, approved, merged, closed) from a real GitHub repository into a clear Mattermost message. Verify GitHub's signature, relay deliveries to a local n8n, and check the ping before you rely on it.

lessons.title: Incident management with n8n: severity, escalation, resolution
lessons.summary: Turn a flood of repeated alerts into one incident with a severity, escalate when nobody acknowledges, and post the resolution, on a real outage. The lab includes the full n8n and Mattermost stack.

lessons.title: Intelligent alerting: grouping, suppression and urgency scoring
lessons.summary: Turn a 200-alert flood into three clear Mattermost messages: group and de-duplicate, mute known noise and maintenance windows, score urgency with rules first and AI only for unclear cases, and send a daily "what was noisy" report.

lessons.title: AI summaries in n8n workflows, safely
lessons.summary: Add AI to real automations with n8n: summaries of failed deployments and incidents with secrets removed first, logs treated as untrusted text, drafts labelled, and a human who decides.

lessons.title: AI incident triage: ranked hypotheses a human confirms
lessons.summary: A bad deploy triggers an alert; n8n gathers the deploy history and logs, and an AI model drafts three ranked hypotheses with exact evidence lines. The on-call engineer checks them, rejects a wrong guess, confirms the cause and rolls back.

lessons.title: Build an AI ops agent in n8n with tools, memory and guardrails
lessons.summary: Ask "why is payments slow?" and let an n8n AI Agent check health, metrics, logs and the runbook with read-only tools. Risky actions become requests: a separate approval workflow restarts only after a human clicks.

lessons.title: AI in CI/CD: explain a failed pipeline and suggest the fix
lessons.summary: When a GitHub Actions job fails, n8n reads the failed log, an AI model explains it in plain words and suggests a fix, and the team sees the draft in Mattermost. The AI explains and suggests; it never merges or deploys.

lessons.title: Review pull requests with AI, a human still decides
lessons.summary: On a real GitHub repository, n8n fetches each new pull request’s diff, an AI model drafts a review with risks on exact lines, a checklist and questions, and posts it to the PR. It catches a prompt injection hidden in the code, and never approves or merges: the reviewer does.

lessons.title: Go further with n8n: the complete automation course
lessons.summary: You have seen what n8n does for AI and DevOps. Here is what the dedicated n8n course adds, if you want to go deeper.
lessons.articleMd:
You have just used n8n to send deployment notifications from CI, follow pull requests in your team chat, summarise failures with AI and run an AI ops agent that asks before it acts. That is enough to start automating your own team's work.

If you want to go deeper, **AI-Powered DevOps Automation with n8n** is our complete course on the tool. It is optional: nothing in this masterclass depends on it.

## What the complete n8n course adds
- **Your own automation stack:** n8n and Mattermost with Docker Compose, locally or on an AWS VM built with Terraform.
- **Alerts people trust:** Kubernetes crash loops, stuck rollouts and unschedulable pods, one clear message per problem, plus a daily health report.
- **Incident management:** repeated alerts become one incident with a severity, escalation when nobody acknowledges, and a resolved message.
- **Failing safely:** retries, fallback paths, error workflows and node-by-node debugging.
- **Scheduled reports** your team reads every morning.
- **n8n in production:** Postgres, queue mode with workers, the encryption key, backups, upgrades and rollback.
- **Advanced patterns:** signed webhooks, idempotency, rate limits, pagination and loop guards.

Every hands-on lesson comes with its lab and a short quiz.

[See the complete n8n course]({{course:n8n-automation}})

lessons.title: What MCP is and why every platform adopted it
lessons.summary: The Model Context Protocol: the problem it solves, its three roles, why GitHub, AWS, Microsoft, Atlassian and Slack adopted it, and how an agent acts as a scoped delegate.

lessons.title: Inside MCP: tools, resources, prompts and transports
lessons.summary: What an MCP server offers and how agents discover it: tools, resources and prompts, stdio and Streamable HTTP, and how a remote server checks who you are with OAuth.

lessons.title: Build your first MCP server and connect real agents
lessons.summary: Write an MCP server in Python with one tool, one resource and one prompt, run it with Docker Compose, test it in the MCP Inspector, and connect Claude Code and Codex to it.

sections.title: LLMOps: run AI applications in production

lessons.title: LLMOps day to day: what you manage once an AI app is live
lessons.summary: What changes from classic ML, and what you manage every day: prompts as production configuration, model versions, evaluation, knowledge freshness, cost, latency and feedback.

lessons.title: Who builds a RAG system, and who runs it
lessons.summary: The developer side, the operations side and the shared middle of a RAG system, and the four LLMOps pipelines: ingest, deploy, evaluate and observe.

lessons.title: Managed AI or self-hosted: Bedrock, Foundry or Ollama
lessons.summary: Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry versus Ollama on your own VM or cluster: who manages what, the real trade-offs, and four questions that decide.

lessons.title: Operating and securing AI in production
lessons.summary: Versions, freshness, the four LLMOps pipelines, observability, drift, prompt injection, data leakage and least privilege: the operations side of running AI.

lessons.title: Continue your learning journey
lessons.summary: Where to go from here: the AWS masterclass for multi-cloud AI, the complete n8n course for automation, and the free VS Code masterclass.
lessons.articleMd:
You can now build, secure and run AI systems on Azure: models, RAG, agents that fix real problems, MCP servers and AI in your pipelines. Here are three optional next steps, depending on where you want to grow.

## Multi-cloud AI: AI for DevOps on AWS
Many teams run on more than one cloud. The AWS masterclass builds the same kinds of systems with Amazon Bedrock, Knowledge Bases and AWS's identity and guardrail tools. The AI foundations are the same, so you can go straight to the hands-on modules.

[See the AWS masterclass]({{course:ai-for-devops-aws}})

## Automation: AI-Powered DevOps Automation with n8n
The complete n8n course goes far beyond the module you took here: Kubernetes alerts, incident management with escalation, scheduled reports and n8n in production.

[See the n8n course]({{course:n8n-automation}})

## Productivity: Visual Studio Code Masterclass for DevOps and AI (free)
Work faster in the editor you use every day: remote development on cloud VMs, Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform tooling, and AI coding assistants.

[See the VS Code masterclass]({{course:vscode-masterclass}})
